title: Set up a sandboxed coding agent with rule checks
summary: Gojko Adzic shared a Claude Code starter setup from his Votito project; he reports its planner cut token spending by about 80%.
agent_role: Claude Code plans and implements changes inside a sealed container, while fixed scripts approve commands, check code and run the workflow steps. The human sets the rules and approves plans.
outcome: Author reports the orchestrator reduced token spend by around 80% compared with a bare Claude workflow on Votito.
what_they_did: The author packaged the setup he built for his product Votito. Claude Code runs in a sealed container that only sees the project folder. A rule script auto-approves or blocks shell commands, and a code checker runs after every edit. A generator turns a plan into a multi-agent workflow so routine steps run without the model.
how_it_went: He reports the orchestrator cut token spending by around 80% compared with running Claude workflows on their own.
worth_knowing: He suggests asking the agent to add a new rule each time it asks you for approval or you repeat the same review feedback.
prompt: Set up my project [repo URL] so you work inside a container that only sees the project folder. Write a list of allowed and blocked shell commands for this project, and add a check that runs the code style checker after every file you edit. Then, for my next change, [describe change], write a step-by-step plan with test checkpoints. Show me the plan and wait for my approval before writing code.

curation.rationale: A starter kit drawn from a real project, with one reported result (about 80% lower token spend), but the post mostly describes features rather than a worked outcome.
